question: Should autoreview make persistent cross-provider panel defaults and private run telemetry part of the shared skill’s supported default contract, or should provider-specific routing remain an explicit opt-in workflow?
rationale: The patch defines user-facing default models, effort levels, service tiers, fallback consent, credential boundaries, and persisted local state; these are durable product and support commitments rather than a mechanical correction.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow supported contract
options.body: Define the stable defaults, opt-in and fallback semantics, credential-isolation guarantees, and telemetry retention behavior, then require focused live proof before merge.

options.title: Keep routing explicitly opt-in
options.body: Retain the existing shared default and publish provider-specific profiles as documented opt-in usage until a broader support contract is approved.

options.title: Split telemetry from panel routing
options.body: Review the model/auth default changes separately from local history persistence so each contract has focused compatibility and security evidence.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow supported contract
recommendation.body: Define the stable defaults, opt-in and fallback semantics, credential-isolation guarantees, and telemetry retention behavior, then require focused live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent readiness work covers the closest overlapping contracts, so this contributor is the best available low-confidence routing candidate from the supplied context.
